bib.title: A Deep Reinforced Model for Abstractive Summarization
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v3; ICLR 2018 poster per ledger)

question: Can a decoder with intra-attention and a training objective mixing maximum likelihood with self-critical RL produce readable, higher-ROUGE abstractive summaries of long documents without repeated phrases?
hypothesis: Combining the maximum-likelihood (conditional language model) loss with RL rewards reduces exposure bias and keeps summaries readable, whereas optimising ROUGE alone with RL can game the metric.
contributions: Intra-temporal attention over the encoder and intra-decoder attention over previously generated output to cut repetition
Mixed objective combining teacher-forcing ML loss with self-critical policy gradient
First end-to-end abstractive model on the NYT dataset; state-of-the-art ROUGE on CNN/Daily Mail; human evaluation of readability

method.summary: Bi-LSTM encoder, single LSTM decoder with intra-temporal encoder attention, intra-decoder attention, a copy/generate switch (pointer) and shared embedding/output weights. Trained first with ML (teacher forcing with 25% own-token feeding), then initialised from the best ML model and fine-tuned with self-critical RL (reward ROUGE-L) or the mixed ML+RL loss. Trigram repetition is blocked in beam search at test time.
method.task: abstractive multi-sentence summarisation of news articles (CNN/Daily Mail, NYT)

datasets.name: CNN/Daily Mail (modified, Nallapati et al. 2016 preprocessing)
datasets.preprocessing: input limited to 800 tokens and output to 100; average input 632 and output 53 tokens; named entities anonymised and replaced back for scoring

datasets.name: New York Times annotated corpus (own splits)
datasets.split: chronological: first 90% train, next 5% val, last 5% test
datasets.preprocessing: drop documents lacking text, abstract or headline; input = headline+byline+article joined by special tokens; Stanford tokenizer; lowercase; numbers -> 0; abstracts split into sentences on semicolons; average 549 input and 40 output tokens after 800/100 caps; Stanford NER used to supervise the pointer for PERSON/LOCATION/ORGANIZATION/MISC entities and OOV tokens

datasets.name: NYT (Durrett et al. 2016 splits)
datasets.size: about 6x smaller than the authors' NYT set, longer summaries

models.name: ML / RL / ML+RL with intra-attention
models.architecture: bi-LSTM encoder (two 200-d LSTMs), one 400-d LSTM decoder, pointer switch, tied embeddings
models.init_from: RL and ML+RL initialised from best ML model; input embeddings from GloVe
models.vocab: input 150,000 tokens, output 50,000 (most frequent in train)

models.name: Lead-3, SummaRuNNer, words-lvt2k-temp-att, Durrett et al. extractive

training.objective: L_mixed = gamma*L_rl + (1-gamma)*L_ml; L_rl = (r(y_hat) - r(y_sample)) * sum log p(y_sample_t); self-critical baseline is the greedy output; reward = ROUGE-L
training.lr: 0.001 for ML; 0.0001 for RL and ML+RL
training.regularisation: ML stage feeds the model's own previous token with 25% probability instead of ground truth (reduces exposure bias, Venkatraman et al. 2015)

other.ground_truth_pointer: u_t=1 when y_t is OOV or a predefined named entity

inference.max_tokens: 100 output tokens (inferred from the output cap in the datasets)
inference.samples: one run per model; no seeds reported

parameters.trigram_blocking: p(y_t)=0 if y_t would repeat a trigram already in the current beam's output

metrics.name: ROUGE recall (limited length)
metrics.definition: summary truncated to ground-truth length; used for the Durrett NYT comparison

metrics.name: Human readability and relevance
metrics.definition: 1-10 scores, 100 random CNN/DM test examples, 5 Mechanical Turk raters each, blind to model and ground truth

eval.protocol: Ablate intra-attention with ML first, pick best, then compare RL vs ML+RL. No significance test or seeds reported. Comparison with See et al. 2017 is indirect (different preprocessing).

availability.data: CNN/DM and NYT public; NYT splits described in appendix

evidence.quote: a learning rate α of 0.001 for ML training and 0.0001 for RL and ML+RL training

limits: Models are small LSTMs (200/400-d) trained from scratch; no parameter counts, compute, steps, seeds or dropout reported.
No ablation of the trigram blocking or of gamma; gamma=0.9984 stated without a sweep.
Comparison with See et al. 2017 is indirect because preprocessing differs; the claim to beat them rests on their model losing to their own lead-3.
Human study is 100 examples and has no inter-rater agreement or significance test.
Abstract's 41.16 ROUGE-1 comes from the RL-only model whose summaries are the least readable; the mixed model scores 39.87.
Intra-attention helps only on long outputs (CNN/DM), not on NYT (Fig 2).
The RL-trained example (Table 3) ends in degenerate fragments, evidence of metric gaming.

terms.definition: the network has knowledge of the ground truth sequence up to the next token during training but does not have such supervision when testing, hence accumulating errors as it predicts the sequence
RL training that uses the reward of the greedy output as the baseline for the sampled sequence, needing no critic network
